D-53 on web: a disconnected device wipes its data — only on explicit device_revoked from the server (REST 401 { error: { code: "device_revoked", reason } } parsed by classifyApiFailure without a token refresh; sync error frame + close 4410 → SyncClient deviceRevoked, status revoked, no reconnect); any reason (user, password_change, recovery, token_reuse, account_deleted) wipes; plain 401 unauthorized and network errors keep the old keep-data sign-out
nodes.rationale: Only the server can tell a revocation from a session that simply ended, so the wipe is bound to an explicit, unambiguous signal; an expired token, a proxy 401 or a network failure must never destroy local data.

nodes.label: api/client.ts: 401 device_revoked recognised by classifyApiFailure (shared) — no token refresh; TokenSource.deviceRevoked(reason) tells the app and DeviceRevokedError is thrown (checkRevoked)
Sync side of D-53: server error frame + WebSocket close 4410 → SyncClient emits deviceRevoked, status revoked, never reconnects; web runtime calls wipeRevokedDevice

wipeRevokedDevice() (auth/session.ts), run once even when REST and sync both signal: deletes the account DB (documents, outbox, notebook keys, attachment cache, ds.unsaved.* tails), session and recovery key, decrypted attachments in memory (forgetDecryptedAttachments), the tab's share keys
nodes.rationale: REST and the sync socket can report the same revocation almost simultaneously; a single shared promise keeps the wipe idempotent.
